what: THE ONE PLACE THE PROJECT'S EXPECTED CHECK AND FAILURE COUNTS LIVE. Written at Batch DE. `check_de.gd` reads this after every battery and reports; `docs/state.md` and `CLAUDE.md` POINT AT IT AND DO NOT RESTATE IT, because a second copy of a number is this project's oldest recurring defect.
how_a_row_moves: A BASELINE MOVES ONLY IN THE BATCH THAT CAUSES THE MOVEMENT, AND THE CHANGELOG SAYS WHY. Otherwise the table drifts into whatever the code happens to do.

fields.kind: suite | gate | scene | harness — chooses how the log is parsed.
fields.checks: [lo, hi] expected check count, or null when the target reports no readable count. THE FLOOR IS ASSERTED AND THE CEILING IS NOT: a FALLING count is an error, a RISING one is a notice.
fields.fails: [lo, hi] expected FAILURE count, or null when unreadable. THE POLARITY INVERTS: a RISING failure count is an error (the 48th failure among 47), a FALLING one is a notice.
fields.checks_obs / fails_obs: HOW MANY READINGS THE ROW RESTS ON. A band is a claim about a distribution nobody has characterised and the readings behind it are part of the claim — an's nine-observation band was exceeded on its tenth. THE COUNTING RULE: one per battery reading the record names from DC forward, plus DE's THREE (before on unmodified HEAD, after, and the final acceptance run) = 6, with named exceptions counted low where there is any doubt. A row whose FAILURE evidence differs from its CHECK evidence carries its own number — see test_batch_bo and test_rune_battle.
fields.expect: optional: a verdict substring that must appear, for a target that reports no counts at all.
fields.flake: optional: a KNOWN flake and its observed rate. Its failure count is carried as a band for that reason.
fields.note: optional: why this row is what it is.

check_di.note: NEW AT DI, AND THE ROW IS A RATCHET RATHER THAN A MEASUREMENT. §1 counts `_apply_status` call sites out of battle.gd's own text with a BALANCED-PAREN WALK and asserts `src` coverage never falls below the floor the last batch left (DI 99, DJ 106) and that no site passes an explicit `null`. IT WALKS RATHER THAN GREPS BECAUSE THE FIGURE DI INHERITED — 53 of 204, in docs/state.md and in DH's own comment — WAS A GREP AND WAS WRONG: 25 of the 204 calls wrap across lines and twelve of those already passed a source, so real coverage before DI was 63. §2 measures Harvest's ally term on a SEEDED pair (both arms draw the same stream, per DD's rule) and asserts the ratio is 1.5 exactly, with a self-vs-self arm and an enemy-source arm as the negative halves. §3 drives the changed call sites through real casts. §4 ASSERTED THE COMPANION GAP DI FOUND AND DELIBERATELY DID NOT CLOSE, AND DJ RULED ON IT: its third assertion moved from 1.0 (a companion-opened wound paid nothing) to 1.5 (it pays what a hero's pays). THE FIRST TWO DID NOT MOVE — `heroes` still does not hold the companion and `_hero_side()` still does. Count is unchanged at 44 across the ruling, over 10 readings.

check_dj.note: NEW AT DJ, AND §5's SITE RATCHET MOVED OUT AT DK. §1 reads Harvest's ally loop out of battle.gd's own text and asserts it walks the written-out union `heroes + companions` — NOT `_hero_side()`, which filters `dead` and would silently stop paying for a wound a FALLEN hero opened. §2 measures the payout twice: hand-stamped to a companion (1.5, the same band check_di §2 gives a hero) and on a wound opened by a REAL `_companion_strike` (1.125 — one of four wounds is the ally's), so a site that stops passing its source reds even though the arithmetic still works. §3 drives four of the seven companion call sites live and asserts the other three off the source, and SAYS WHICH IS WHICH. §4 IS THE NEGATIVE CONTROL ON THE COLLECTION ITSELF: a fallen hero's wound must still pay 1.0 of a living one — DI's proposed one-word `_hero_side()` fix passes §2 and reads 0.6664 here. §5 KEEPS the count of no-op `is_companion` filters over `heroes` at 23, which is DJ's own finding and which no other gate asserts — and DK is what that count exists for: DK widened four ally read sites to `_hero_side()`, a filter on any of them would have started removing the beast, none carried one, and the count holding at 23 is how that is checkable. §6 asserts the wrong belief is gone from the four LIVE prose sites, and deliberately does not sweep the changelog or the batch reports, which are history. **54 → 43 AT DK, PREDICTED**: DJ pinned all ELEVEN bare-`heroes` ally-worded effects by their own read lines with a message asking the next batch to RULE; DK ruled on all eleven, and `check_dk` §1 pins both resulting populations in both directions. The eleven were DELETED rather than re-pointed — keeping them would be two copies of one fact in two gates. COUNTED LOW ON PURPOSE: one reading supports the 43, and the 54 it replaces rested on three.

check_dk.note: NEW AT DK. THE GATE FOR “four ally-worded effects reach the beast, and seven say hero because they cannot”. DJ §2 swept eleven ally-worded effects walking bare `heroes` and ruled on none; DK ruled, and they split FOUR and SEVEN. §1 pins BOTH populations by their own read lines and asserts each in the direction that can break it — a widened site going back to bare `heroes` is a REGRESSION, and a narrow site widening makes its `hero` text wrong. It also re-asserts that Harvest still spells its union out, because a receive-site's `dead` answer is not Harvest's. §2 IS THE LIVE HALF AND IT SUMMONS A REAL BEAR: Sanctuary heals it 1200 of a 10000 body, Hold the Line leaves it 20 Break from a 40-BD blow (exactly the base 50% cut) and holds it at 1 HP through a lethal one, Rally turns a 1000 heal into 1300, and the Field Medic's pool holds it once poisoned. SANCTUARY AND HOLD THE LINE ARE DRIVEN THROUGH `_resolve_special`; RALLY AND FIELD MEDIC LIVE INSIDE `_resolve`'s block branch and `_run_battle`'s turn-start block and cannot be called, so those evaluate the loop's own expression live — WHICH IS WHICH IS SAID RATHER THAN BLURRED. §2 ALSO CARRIES THE NEGATIVE CONTROL AND IT IS NOT OPTIONAL: the failure DK repairs was invisible in every battery ever run, so a check that passes on the fixed tree proves nothing. It empties `companions` for the length of one arm — precisely the pre-DK collection — and asserts the beast is untouched (Sanctuary heals it 0, Hold the Line leaves the full 40). §4 IS THE BATCH'S ACTUAL CARE: Tank and Spank was the fifth candidate to widen and was MEASURED instead. `empower` attaches to a companion cleanly and pays it nothing, because a beast's blows resolve through `_companion_hit`, its own damage path, which reads none of the hero strike loop's multipliers — 40 seeded blows read 34392 against 34392, ratio 1.0000. THE RULING IS PINNED AS THAT MEASUREMENT rather than as an assertion, so the day `_companion_hit` grows an `empower` read the gate says the ruling is stale instead of staying quietly true. §5 asserts the eleven texts — seven `hero`, four `ally` — in both directions, plus that no §2 text still carries its pre-DK wording. §6 asserts CV §4's false test is gone from CLAUDE.md, that master.html no longer flags Hold the Line as excluding companions, and that the glossary no longer lists Tank and Spank's Empower as an `ally` effect. Gate takes ~5s. ONE READING SUPPORTS THE 64.

check_dl.note: BATCH DL's gate. §1 pins BOTH of Rallying Shout's clauses by their own read lines (the Pressure walk is `_hero_side()`, the resource walk is bare `heroes` plus its `resource_name` guard); §2 measures 30 Pressure shed on a live summoned Ursus; §3 is the NEGATIVE CONTROL — `companions` emptied for one cast, which is exactly the pre-DL collection, and the beast sheds 0; §4 measures the clause that did NOT move (the beast banks 0 resource, and `max_resource` is asserted NON-zero because DK recorded it as 0 and that was false).

check_dm.note: BATCH DM's gate, and it is the gate for a batch that WIDENED NOTHING. §1 reads all six of DL's split-clause cards CLAUSE BY CLAUSE and pins fourteen collection-bearing clauses plus two self clauses by their own read lines — AND IT ANCHORS ON THE CLAUSE AND SEARCHES BACKWARD FOR THE WALK, because FIVE sites in `battle.gd` spell `heroes.filter(func(he): return not he.dead and not he.is_companion)` byte for byte, so a forward `find` from the walk reads the wrong site four times in five (the fault that bit DL at War Stomp's guard, fixed in the DIRECTION rather than in the fragment). The shared-walk COUNT is printed live and the assertion is the property (`> 1`) rather than a number — this gate asserted TWO on its first run and caught its own author. §2 IS THE LIVE HALF ON A REAL SUMMONED URSUS and it MEASURES all five recorded reasons rather than asserting them: `_gain_faith` pays the beast 0 and a hero 2 off the same call; `wrath` and `battle_shout` each attach to the beast cleanly and move 40 seeded blows by ratio 1.0000 (DK's Tank and Spank instrument pointed at two more statuses); the summon's `next_time` is INF and it is outside `_next_unit()`'s walk, which is what makes every per-turn clause hero; and Bulwark, Consecrated Ground, Divine Wrath, Sacred Resolve and Battle Shout each reach their caster and NOT the beast. §2 also measures HOLD THE LINE'S `undying` CLAUSE, which nothing had ever pinned — `check_dk`'s entry covers `hold_bd` only — and the beast holds at 1 HP through a lethal blow. AND IT MEASURES THE CLAUSE DM'S TEXT MOVED: one Battle Shout, EXACTLY ONE unit paid, caster +5 Rage, beast 0. §4 asserts the six cards' words in both directions plus the four prose surfaces DM corrected (three `master.html` copies and one glossary copy of Consecrated Ground's Faith drip, which said `ally` for a payload `_gain_faith` refuses outright). §5 asserts the thread's close is written down. SIX NEGATIVE CONTROLS WERE RUN AND ALL SIX BIT: the two pre-DM card wordings restored (2 and 3 failures), the two prose surfaces reverted to `ally` (2 each), Bulwark's loop WIDENED to `_hero_side()` (2), and Hold the Line's `undying` NARROWED to bare `heroes` (2). Gate takes ~40s. ONE READING SUPPORTS THE 92.

test_batch_at.note: FOUND BY THE DG BATTERY DISAGREEING WITH DG'S OWN PREDICTION, AND PREVIOUSLY UNRECORDED. The three exclusive-pair reds are DELETED at DG §2 (470 -> 467, part of the sanctioned fall of six); this row's remaining ceiling of 1 is a DIFFERENT and NEW failure. IT IS NOT DG's: DG's only edits to this file were three deleted file-reading assertions, which consume no RNG, and the check count landed exactly on prediction. THE ±10% DAMAGE ROLL ALONE DOES NOT EXPLAIN 2.40 — modelled over 200,000 trials, ten summed casts a side put the 5th-95th percentile at 2.08-2.26 and P(over the 2.35 ceiling) at 0.1%, about one run in a thousand. So there is a SECOND random term. THE SUITE'S OWN `_spawn` NAMES THE CANDIDATE, on the very helper this check calls: 'THE CRIT IS THE THIRD COIN AND ON THIS SPEC IT IS THE WORST ONE: Runaway Resonance adds +1% crit PER STACK, so a same-cast-at-0-vs-12 comparison silently compares 10% crit against 22% crit.' The fixture passes crit:-10.0, which removes the BASE and not the PER-STACK term, so the two populations differ in crit chance as well as in the curve the check means to measure. A model carrying the FULL differential over-predicts (32% red against 1 in 18 observed), so the live term is smaller than that and larger than zero, and ITS SIZE IS NOT ESTABLISHED — do not guess it. THE FIX IS THE DD SHAPE, WHICH DD APPLIED TWICE IN THIS SUITE AND DID NOT REACH THIS ONE: seed both blows of the compared pair, or set crit_bonus back as the file's own comment says checks that care must do. DO NOT WIDEN THE BAND — the band IS the question. DELIBERATELY LEFT FOR ITS OWN BATCH: one flake at a time is how the effect stays attributable, and `bo`'s and `test_rune_battle`'s are both still open.

test_rune_battle.note: FOUND BY `check_de` ON ITS FIRST ACCEPTANCE RUN AND PREVIOUSLY UNRECORDED. Its CHECK count is rock steady at 97 across all 15 readings — only the failure moves, which is the flake signature CLAUDE.md names. READINGS: clean in DE's before- and after-batteries, RED in the final acceptance battery, RED on the next ad-hoc run, then TEN CONSECUTIVE CLEAN runs on an idle machine. BOTH REDS LANDED UNDER LOAD, which is a hypothesis and not a finding — the assertion's own comment says the snapshot 'is the one that cannot race', so a race is the thing to look at first. THE FIX IS THE `at`/`bo` SHAPE (seed the draw, or assert on the snapshot alone) AND IT IS DELIBERATELY LEFT FOR ITS OWN BATCH: one flake at a time is how the effect stays attributable. SEEDED AT DF §0, per-site: `_seeded()` immediately before the forced hit and nowhere else, so the other 96 checks keep their own stream. THE BAND IS DELIBERATELY NOT TIGHTENED — two clean post-seed readings cannot retire a rate measured over fifteen, and tightening on that evidence is the same fault as writing a band from too few readings, in the opposite direction. The failure message now carries the state the forced hit happened in (battle_over, both units' liveness, the target's fire resist, the pierce fraction), so the NEXT red says what was missing instead of only that it was missing.
